paras: The Luna Park restaurant riot was a fight at the Cafe Neapolitan in Luna Park, Pittsburg, Pennsylvania, on the evening of August 22, 1905, that began when waiters refused to serve Charles Julius Miller, a Black visitor from Chicago, and grew into what the dispatch called a "desperate race riot" of about two hundred people. Miller was seriously injured, several others were sent to hospitals, and between fifteen and about fifty people were arrested. A single wire dispatch carried the story to white and Black papers from New York to Washington State.

Miller was employed in the registry department of the Chicago post office and was in Pittsburg for the national convention of the colored Knights of Pythias. According to most versions of the dispatch, he entered the cafe with a Black woman, though the New-York Tribune's text does not mention her.

Waiters refused to serve Miller and ordered him out. In the Tribune's wording Miller then "abused" the waiter, while other versions said he "became abusive." One of the waiters tried to strike him with a chair, and Miller drew a revolver; "a large number of shots" were fired before the weapon was taken from him. His friends came to his aid, and a free-for-all fight followed in which, by the dispatch's count, two hundred people took part.

In the longer version of the dispatch, a riot call was sent in. Miller, described as seriously injured, and several others were taken to hospitals. The dispatch did not say how Miller was hurt, whether anyone was struck by the shots, or the race of the waiters and of the others injured.

The Tribune put the number arrested at fifteen, while the St. Louis Palladium, the Colorado Statesman and the Walla Walla Evening Statesman gave about fifty. No report of charges, a court hearing, Miller's later condition or any response from the Pythian convention appears in the coverage.

The New-York Tribune printed the story on its front page on August 23 under the headline "Pittsburg Race Riot," with the deck "Fight Because Waiter Would Not Serve Negro in Restaurant." The Louisville Courier-Journal ran it on August 29 as a Pittsburg special to the St. Louis Globe-Democrat, headed "Refusal to Wait on Negroes Causes Riot." The same day the Walla Walla Evening Statesman printed a shortened version as "Race War In Hashery," under a Pittsburg dateline of August 29 that marks it as a late reprint of the same dispatch. That abridgement dropped the waiter's chair, so that Miller's abuse led directly to his revolver. Every white version followed the restaurant side's sequence of refusal, abuse and gunfire, and none carried a statement from Miller or his friends.

Two Black weeklies reprinted the dispatch nearly word for word. The St. Louis Palladium put it on its front page on August 26 under "Refusal to Wait on Negro Starts Riot" and closed it with the line "I Told You So—Palladium," without saying what it had predicted. The Colorado Statesman ran the full text without comment on September 2. Neither paper added a correspondent's account or an editorial on the case.
The versions differ on the number arrested, fifteen in the Tribune's first report against about fifty in the longer text the later reprints share, and nothing in the coverage settles which is right.

reader.title: Luna Park restaurant riot
bases: A Black patron refused service was ordered out and struck at with a chair by a waiter, and the quarrel became a 'race riot' of about two hundred people in which he was seriously injured (A1, A2); it was a two-sided melee in which Miller fired a revolver, so the label is a close call (see flags).
All five texts are copies or abridgements of one Pittsburg dispatch of Aug. 22 (A1, A2, A3, A4, A5); no local Pittsburg report or independent account was found.

accounts.label: Pittsburg wire dispatch
accounts.gist: Waiters refused to serve Miller; ordered out, he became abusive; a waiter swung at him with a chair, he drew a revolver and shots were fired; his friends joined in and a free-for-all among two hundred people followed, with Miller seriously injured.

accounts.label: Walla Walla abridgement
accounts.gist: Shortened version omitting the waiter's chair, so that Miller's abuse leads directly to his drawing a revolver.

framing.detail: The Tribune headed it 'Pittsburg Race Riot' with the deck 'Fight Because Waiter Would Not Serve Negro in Restaurant', and the Courier-Journal 'Refusal to Wait on Negroes Causes Riot', both placing the refusal at the start.
The Walla Walla paper's 'Race War In Hashery' cut the waiter's chair, leaving Miller's abuse and revolver as the start of the fight.
The Palladium ran the dispatch unchanged under 'Refusal to Wait on Negro Starts Riot' and appended only 'I Told You So—Palladium.', a remark whose target is not explained.
The Colorado Statesman reprinted the full dispatch without comment.

versions.value: About fifty, after a riot call

conflicts.note: The Tribune text is the earliest; the fifty figure appears in the longer version the later reprints share. Neither can be preferred on these texts.
The Walla Walla text is word for word the same dispatch, so the Aug. 29 dateline reflects a late reprint, not a second event.

versions.value: Miller entered with a Negro woman

conflicts.note: Omission in the Tribune text rather than a contradiction.

record_check.dossier: Attempted blow with a chair, a free-for-all fight, and shots fired by Miller; no one is reported killed and no gunshot wound is reported. 'killing' is unsupported; 'shooting' was by Miller.
Miller is described as 'a negro' / 'a Negro'.
Waiters of the Cafe Neapolitan began it; a free-for-all of about two hundred followed. Who injured Miller is not stated.
1905-08-22; the later date comes from the Aug. 29 dateline of a late reprint.
One waiter 'attempted to strike' Miller with a chair; about two hundred engaged in the riot; fifteen or about fifty arrested.
The dispatch says only that waiters refused to serve him and that he was abusive when ordered out.

info: Cafe Neapolitan, Luna Park, Pittsburg (the Palladium headline calls it a suburb of Pittsburg)
Charles Julius Miller, described as a Negro employed in the registry department of the Chicago post office, in Pittsburg for the national convention of the colored Knights of Pythias
None of a crime; the dispatch says that when ordered out Miller 'abused' the waiter or 'became abusive'
Waiters of the Cafe Neapolitan (race not stated); one waiter tried to strike Miller with a chair; a free-for-all followed when Miller's friends joined in
No report of charges, a hearing, or Miller's later condition was found

sources.note: Earliest text, 'By Telegraph', Pittsburg Aug. 22: 200 in race riot at Luna Park; waiter's chair, Miller's revolver; fifteen arrested; no mention of a woman companion.
quotes: Waiters refused to serve him, and Miller, when ordered out by the waiter, abused him. One of the waiters attempted to strike Miller with a chair, and he drew a revolver.
